keywords: Simplify and solve rational expressions while preserving every restriction from the original form.

This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use rational expressions and restrictions repair to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use radicals and rational exponents repair to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use function notation and graph reading repair to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.label: Lesson
keywords: Calculate and interpret average rate of change as output change per input change and as the slope of a secant line.

Average rate of change from a to b is [f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a), the slope of the secant line through the endpoint values. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use average rate of change to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

Multiplying outputs scales vertically; replacing x by cx divides horizontal coordinates by c. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use vertical and horizontal scaling to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

Power functions f(x)=ax^p connect positive, negative, and fractional exponent behavior. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use power functions and dominant behavior to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

Identify removable discontinuities caused by common factors and distinguish formula equivalence from function equality.

A common factor creates a removable discontinuity: the original function follows the simplified curve but omits one point. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use equivalent formulas, different functions, and holes to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Vertical asymptotes and local behavior
records.description: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.

An uncancelled denominator zero often creates a vertical asymptote with unbounded one-sided behavior. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use vertical asymptotes and local behavior to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Horizontal asymptotes and end behavior
records.description: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.

Horizontal asymptotes describe rational end behavior through leading-degree comparison. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use horizontal asymptotes and end behavior to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Slant and polynomial asymptotes
records.description: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.

Polynomial division reveals a nonhorizontal asymptote when a rational numerator has higher degree. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use slant and polynomial asymptotes to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Intercepts and sign charts
records.description: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.

A rational function has constant sign between numerator zeros and denominator zeros. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use intercepts and sign charts to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Complete rational graph construction
records.description: Construct a complete rational graph using domain, discontinuities, asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected values.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Construct a complete rational graph using domain, discontinuities, asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected values.

A complete rational graph combines domain, holes, vertical and end asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected points. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use complete rational graph construction to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Rational equations and function intersections
records.description: Solve rational equations and intersections exactly or numerically while rejecting excluded candidates.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve rational equations and intersections exactly or numerically while rejecting excluded candidates.

Rational intersections satisfy f(x)=g(x), but denominator clearing creates candidates that must be checked in the original domains. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use rational equations and function intersections to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Rational inequalities
records.description: Solve rational inequalities using critical values, sign intervals, and correct endpoint inclusion.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve rational inequalities using critical values, sign intervals, and correct endpoint inclusion.

Rational inequalities are solved by critical-value sign intervals rather than unsafe cross multiplication. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use rational inequalities to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Variation and rational models
records.description: Build and interpret direct, inverse, joint, and combined variation models with meaningful parameters and domains.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Build and interpret direct, inverse, joint, and combined variation models with meaningful parameters and domains.

Variation language describes direct, inverse, joint, and combined proportional structure. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use variation and rational models to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Partial-fraction structure
records.description: Decompose proper rational functions with factorable denominators into simpler component fractions and verify recombination.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Decompose proper rational functions with factorable denominators into simpler component fractions and verify recombination.

Partial fractions rewrite a proper rational function as a sum of simpler components determined by denominator factors. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use partial-fraction structure to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Additive versus multiplicative change
records.description: Distinguish linear, exponential, and neither patterns by comparing equal-input differences, ratios, and percent changes.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Distinguish linear, exponential, and neither patterns by comparing equal-input differences, ratios, and percent changes.

Constant first differences indicate additive linear change; constant ratios indicate multiplicative exponential change. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use additive versus multiplicative change to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Exponential functions and parameters
records.description: Analyze f(x)=ab^x by interpreting initial value, base, multiplier, percent rate, domain, range, and asymptote.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze f(x)=ab^x by interpreting initial value, base, multiplier, percent rate, domain, range, and asymptote.

In f(x)=ab^x, a is f(0) and b is the one-step output multiplier. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use exponential functions and parameters to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Exponential transformations
records.description: Analyze transformed exponential functions and track asymptotes, domain, range, and feature points.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze transformed exponential functions and track asymptotes, domain, range, and feature points.

Transformed exponentials use the general input-output mapping, with horizontal asymptote y=k. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use exponential transformations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Growth and decay models
records.description: Construct exponential models from an initial value, rate, multiplier, two points, or a known doubling or half-life.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Construct exponential models from an initial value, rate, multiplier, two points, or a known doubling or half-life.

Exponential models can be written from an initial value and rate, multiplier, doubling time, or half-life. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use growth and decay models to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Compound interest and effective rate
records.description: Use periodic compounding models and compare nominal rates, periodic rates, compounding frequency, and effective annual yield.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use periodic compounding models and compare nominal rates, periodic rates, compounding frequency, and effective annual yield.

Periodic compounding uses A=P(1+r/n)^(nt), where r/n is the periodic rate and nt counts periods. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use compound interest and effective rate to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Continuous growth and the number e
records.description: Use A(t)=A0e^(kt) for continuous proportional change and interpret the continuous rate parameter k.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Continuous growth and the number e
Use A(t)=A0e^(kt) for continuous proportional change and interpret the continuous rate parameter k.

The number e arises from the limit of increasingly frequent proportional compounding. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use continuous growth and the number e to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Exponential regression and residuals
records.description: Fit an exponential model to data, interpret parameters, inspect residuals, and evaluate interpolation and extrapolation.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Fit an exponential model to data, interpret parameters, inspect residuals, and evaluate interpolation and extrapolation.

Exponential regression estimates a repeated-change model from imperfect data, and residuals measure observed minus predicted output. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use exponential regression and residuals to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Logistic and bounded growth
records.description: Analyze logistic growth qualitatively and interpret initial value, carrying capacity, growth rate, and inflection behavior.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze logistic growth qualitatively and interpret initial value, carrying capacity, growth rate, and inflection behavior.

A logistic model grows rapidly at first and then slows toward a carrying capacity K. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use logistic and bounded growth to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Logarithms as inverse functions
records.description: Define log base b as the inverse of b^x, convert between forms, and interpret logarithms as exponents.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Define log base b as the inverse of b^x, convert between forms, and interpret logarithms as exponents.

log_b(y)=x exactly when b^x=y; a logarithm is the exponent needed to produce a positive output. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use logarithms as inverse functions to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Logarithmic graphs and transformations
records.description: Analyze transformed logarithmic functions, including domain, range, vertical asymptote, intercepts, and base-dependent direction.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze transformed logarithmic functions, including domain, range, vertical asymptote, intercepts, and base-dependent direction.

A transformed logarithm has a vertical input boundary where its argument equals zero. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use logarithmic graphs and transformations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Logarithm laws
records.description: Derive and apply product, quotient, and power laws while preserving positive-argument domains.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive and apply product, quotient, and power laws while preserving positive-argument domains.

Logarithm laws convert products to sums, quotients to differences, and powers to coefficients. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use logarithm laws to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Solving exponential equations
records.description: Solve exponential equations using common bases, logarithms, and numerical methods, and interpret exact and approximate answers.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve exponential equations using common bases, logarithms, and numerical methods, and interpret exact and approximate answers.

Exponential equations place the unknown in an exponent and are solved by common bases, logarithms, substitution, or numerical methods. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use solving exponential equations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Solving logarithmic equations and interpreting inverse models
records.description: Solve logarithmic equations, reject invalid arguments, and use logarithms to analyze doubling time, half-life, and logarithmic scales.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solving logarithmic equations and interpreting inverse models
Solve logarithmic equations, reject invalid arguments, and use logarithms to analyze doubling time, half-life, and logarithmic scales.

A logarithmic equation must be solved inside the original positive-argument domain. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use solving logarithmic equations and interpreting inverse models to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Systems as intersections and models
records.description: Interpret a system solution as an input-output point satisfying every equation and solve two-variable systems graphically and algebraically.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Interpret a system solution as an input-output point satisfying every equation and solve two-variable systems graphically and algebraically.

A system solution satisfies every equation simultaneously and appears graphically as a common intersection. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use systems as intersections and models to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Nonlinear systems
records.description: Solve systems involving lines, quadratics, circles, rational, exponential, or other nonlinear functions and interpret all real intersections.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve systems involving lines, quadratics, circles, rational, exponential, or other nonlinear functions and interpret all real intersections.

A nonlinear system contains at least one curved relation and may have zero, one, or several intersections. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use nonlinear systems to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Systems of inequalities and feasible regions
records.description: Graph simultaneous inequalities, identify feasible regions, and interpret boundaries and vertices.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Systems of inequalities and feasible regions
Graph simultaneous inequalities, identify feasible regions, and interpret boundaries and vertices.

A system of inequalities describes the intersection of several shaded solution regions. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use systems of inequalities and feasible regions to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Systems in three variables
records.description: Solve and classify three-variable linear systems and interpret their solutions as intersections of planes.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve and classify three-variable linear systems and interpret their solutions as intersections of planes.

A linear equation in three variables describes a plane, and a system seeks their common point, line, plane, or empty intersection. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use systems in three variables to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Matrix notation and operations
records.description: Represent rectangular arrays with matrices and perform dimension-compatible addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Represent rectangular arrays with matrices and perform dimension-compatible addition, scalar multiplication, and matrix multiplication.

A matrix is a rectangular array whose dimensions record row and column counts. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use matrix notation and operations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Augmented matrices and row operations
records.description: Translate linear systems into augmented matrices and justify elementary row operations as equivalent-system transformations.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Translate linear systems into augmented matrices and justify elementary row operations as equivalent-system transformations.

An augmented matrix records a linear system in a fixed variable order. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use augmented matrices and row operations to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Gaussian elimination and echelon form
records.description: Use forward elimination to reach row-echelon form and solve by back-substitution.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use forward elimination to reach row-echelon form and solve by back-substitution.

Gaussian elimination creates row-echelon form by clearing entries below successive pivots. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use gaussian elimination and echelon form to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Gauss-Jordan elimination and reduced row-echelon form
records.description: Reduce matrices to RREF and interpret pivots, free variables, rank, and consistency directly.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Gauss-Jordan elimination and reduced row-echelon form
Reduce matrices to RREF and interpret pivots, free variables, rank, and consistency directly.

Reduced row-echelon form has pivot ones that are the only nonzero entries in their columns. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use gauss-jordan elimination and reduced row-echelon form to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Determinants, singularity, and inverse matrices
records.description: Compute and interpret determinants, identify singular matrices, and solve suitable systems with inverse matrices.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Compute and interpret determinants, identify singular matrices, and solve suitable systems with inverse matrices.

The determinant of a square matrix detects invertibility and geometric area scaling. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use determinants, singularity, and inverse matrices to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Linear transformations and multivariable modeling
records.description: Interpret matrices as transformations of vectors and construct a complete multivariable model using equations, inequalities, and matrices.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Interpret matrices as transformations of vectors and construct a complete multivariable model using equations, inequalities, and matrices.

A matrix transformation sends the standard basis vectors to its columns, determining the image of every vector. This matters because the rest of Precalculus will repeatedly use linear transformations and multivariable modeling to decide what a formula means, what a graph can show, and which conclusions remain valid.

records.title: Directed rotation and coterminal angles
records.description: Represent rotations in standard position and generate all coterminal angles.
records.topicName: Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Represent rotations in standard position and generate all coterminal angles.
Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle

A radar arm begins on the positive x-axis, rotates 765 degrees counterclockwise, then 180 degrees clockwise. Where is its terminal side, and what is the smallest positive coterminal angle? Directed rotations appear in navigation, rotating machinery, phase, circular motion, and complex-number arguments.

records.title: Degree measure and angular coordinates
records.description: Use degrees, revolutions, and degree-minute-second notation to measure and compare rotation.
records.topicName: Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use degrees, revolutions, and degree-minute-second notation to measure and compare rotation.
Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle

A telescope turns from heading 18 degrees 42 minutes to heading 137 degrees 15 minutes. Through what angle did it rotate? DMS is useful when measurements are recorded with angular precision smaller than one degree.

records.title: Radian measure as normalized arc length
records.description: Define radian measure as signed arc length divided by radius and explain why it is independent of circle size.
records.topicName: Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Radian measure as normalized arc length
Define radian measure as signed arc length divided by radius and explain why it is independent of circle size.
Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle

Two circles have radii 2 and 10. On each, an arc has length equal to three times the radius. What angle does each arc subtend? Radians simplify arc length, angular speed, trigonometric graphs, derivatives, and periodic models.

records.title: Arc length and sector area
records.description: Derive and use s=r theta and A=(1/2)r^2 theta for angles measured in radians.
records.topicName: Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive and use s=r theta and A=(1/2)r^2 theta for angles measured in radians.
Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle

A sprinkler waters a sector of radius 12 meters through an angle of 5pi/12. Find the boundary arc length and watered area. Sector formulas model sprinklers, gears, fan blades, circular tracks, camera fields, and rotating swept regions.

records.title: Angular speed and linear speed
records.description: Relate angular speed, radius, and tangential speed using v=r omega.
records.topicName: Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Relate angular speed, radius, and tangential speed using v=r omega.
Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle

A bicycle wheel has radius 0.34 meter and turns at 180 revolutions per minute. Find angular speed in radians per second and bicycle speed in meters per second. The relation supports wheel speedometers, pulleys, gears, turbines, turntables, and orbital motion.

records.title: Wrapping the real line around the unit circle
records.description: Map any real number t to the unit-circle point reached by signed arc length t.
records.topicName: Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Wrapping the real line around the unit circle
Map any real number t to the unit-circle point reached by signed arc length t.
Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
Starting at (1,0), where does traveling an arc length of 17pi/6 counterclockwise place the point? This construction is the bridge from geometric circles to real-valued periodic functions.

records.title: Sine and cosine as coordinate functions
records.description: Define cosine and sine as the x- and y-coordinates of the unit-circle point P(t).
records.topicName: Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Sine and cosine as coordinate functions
Define cosine and sine as the x- and y-coordinates of the unit-circle point P(t).
Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle

A rotating point has unit-circle coordinate P(t)=(-5/13,12/13). Find sin t, cos t, and the quadrant. Coordinate functions model circular position, oscillation, projection, sound, waves, and periodic change.

records.title: Exact values from special triangles
records.description: Derive exact unit-circle values from 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles.
records.topicName: Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive exact unit-circle values from 45-45-90 and 30-60-90 triangles.
Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
Without using a memorized chart, derive sin(pi/3), cos(pi/3), and tan(pi/3). These exact anchors support graph construction, identities, equations, vectors, and triangle solving.

records.title: Reference angles, quadrants, and signs
records.description: Use reference angles and quadrant signs to evaluate trigonometric functions of arbitrary rotations.
records.topicName: Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use reference angles and quadrant signs to evaluate trigonometric functions of arbitrary rotations.
Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
Evaluate sin(23pi/6), cos(23pi/6), and tan(23pi/6) exactly. The same reasoning later generates all solutions to trig equations.

records.title: Tangent and the reciprocal functions
records.description: Define tangent, cotangent, secant, and cosecant from sine and cosine and state domains, signs, periods, and identities.
records.topicName: Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Define tangent, cotangent, secant, and cosecant from sine and cosine and state domains, signs, periods, and identities.
Angles, Radians, and the Unit Circle

A unit-circle point is P=(-8/17,15/17). Find all six trig values and identify which are negative. The six functions provide the language for slope, projection, triangles, identities, and periodic graphs.

records.title: Building the sine graph from circular motion
records.description: Construct y=sin t from the vertical coordinate of a rotating unit-circle point.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Building the sine graph from circular motion
Construct y=sin t from the vertical coordinate of a rotating unit-circle point.

A point starts at (1,0) and rotates counterclockwise one revolution in 8 seconds. Sketch its vertical coordinate against time and label zeros, extrema, and period. Sine models vertical projection, alternating current, sound, tides, and repeated motion.

records.title: Building the cosine graph from circular motion
records.description: Construct y=cos t from the horizontal coordinate of circular motion and compare it with sine.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Building the cosine graph from circular motion
Construct y=cos t from the horizontal coordinate of circular motion and compare it with sine.

A rotating point begins at (1,0). At what inputs does its horizontal coordinate equal its vertical coordinate during one revolution? Cosine naturally models quantities that begin at a maximum or minimum.

records.title: Amplitude, reflection, and midline
records.description: Interpret A and D in y=A sin x+D or y=A cos x+D.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Interpret A and D in y=A sin x+D or y=A cos x+D.
An ocean buoy moves between 1.2 and 4.8 meters above a reference level. Find the midline and amplitude. Amplitude and midline describe tides, temperatures, voltage, vibration, and circular height.

records.title: Period, frequency, and angular frequency
records.description: Relate inside scale B to period, ordinary frequency, and angular frequency.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Relate inside scale B to period, ordinary frequency, and angular frequency.
A piston completes 15 cycles in 6 seconds. Find frequency, period, and angular frequency. Frequency parameters model music, rotation, seasonal cycles, waves, and machinery.

records.title: Phase shift and timing
records.description: Interpret B(x-C) as a horizontal timing shift and recover C from graph or context.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Interpret B(x-C) as a horizontal timing shift and recover C from graph or context.

A seasonal temperature reaches its maximum on day 205 of a 365-day cycle. Write a cosine model phase term with the maximum at day 205. Phase aligns a periodic model with calendar dates, starting positions, or delayed signals.

records.title: The general sinusoidal function
records.description: Build and analyze y=A sin(B(x-C))+D and equivalent cosine forms.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Build and analyze y=A sin(B(x-C))+D and equivalent cosine forms.

A Ferris wheel ranges from 2 to 38 meters, has period 60 seconds, and begins at its lowest point. Write a height model. General sinusoidal models describe Ferris wheels, daylight, tides, seasons, and rotating sensors.

records.title: Tangent and cotangent graphs
records.description: Derive tangent and cotangent graphs from quotient definitions, zeros, asymptotes, and period pi.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive tangent and cotangent graphs from quotient definitions, zeros, asymptotes, and period pi.
Sketch tan x on (-pi/2,3pi/2) using sine and cosine signs rather than memory. Tangent models slopes, perspective, periodic blow-up behavior, and phase response.

records.title: Secant and cosecant graphs
records.description: Construct secant and cosecant graphs as reciprocals of cosine and sine.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Construct secant and cosecant graphs as reciprocals of cosine and sine.
Use the graph of cos x to sketch sec x on [0,2pi], marking all vertices and asymptotes. Reciprocal trig graphs appear in optics, wave geometry, and analytic identities.

records.title: Symmetry, periodicity, and the six-function family
records.description: Compare domains, ranges, parity, periods, zeros, and asymptotes of all six trig functions.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Symmetry, periodicity, and the six-function family
Compare domains, ranges, parity, periods, zeros, and asymptotes of all six trig functions.
Without graphing, decide which trig functions satisfy f(-x)=-f(x) and which satisfy f(-x)=f(x). The family comparison is essential for identities and equation solving.

records.title: Inverse trigonometric functions and branch restrictions
records.description: Define inverse sine, cosine, and tangent using one-to-one branches and principal-value ranges.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Inverse trigonometric functions and branch restrictions
Define inverse sine, cosine, and tangent using one-to-one branches and principal-value ranges.

Why can sin x not have an inverse on all real numbers, and why is [-pi/2,pi/2] a useful restricted domain? Inverse trig functions recover angles in triangles, equations, vectors, and numerical models.

records.title: Basic trigonometric equations
records.description: Solve sin x=k, cos x=k, and tan x=k using exact values, inverse functions, periodicity, and interval restrictions.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve sin x=k, cos x=k, and tan x=k using exact values, inverse functions, periodicity, and interval restrictions.
Solve sin x=1/2 for all real x and then list solutions on [-pi,3pi]. Basic equations locate times, angles, phases, and intersections in periodic models.

records.title: Sinusoidal modeling and regression
records.description: Fit and critique sinusoidal models using amplitude, midline, period, phase, residuals, and domain.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Fit and critique sinusoidal models using amplitude, midline, period, phase, residuals, and domain.

Monthly daylight hours range from 9.1 to 15.3, with a maximum near day 172. Build a first sinusoidal model with period 365. Periodic regression supports climate, tides, daylight, acoustics, and mechanical monitoring.

records.title: Identities, equations, and proof strategy
records.description: Distinguish identities from conditional equations and use valid one-sided transformation strategies.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Distinguish identities from conditional equations and use valid one-sided transformation strategies.

Is (1-cos^2 x)/sin x=sin x an identity? State the exact common domain on which the equality is valid. Identity reasoning supports simplification, equation solving, signal analysis, and later calculus manipulations.

records.title: Reciprocal, quotient, and Pythagorean identities
records.description: Derive and apply the fundamental trig identities from unit-circle coordinates.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive and apply the fundamental trig identities from unit-circle coordinates.
Starting from sin^2 x+cos^2 x=1, derive 1+tan^2 x=sec^2 x and state its domain. The identities provide the algebraic vocabulary for every later trig proof and equation.

records.title: Verifying identities strategically
records.description: Select factoring, common denominators, conjugates, or sine-cosine conversion to verify identities.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Select factoring, common denominators, conjugates, or sine-cosine conversion to verify identities.
Verify (1-cos x)/sin x=sin x/(1+cos x) on the common domain. Proof strategy trains the same structure recognition used in algebra, calculus, and mathematical writing.

records.title: Sum and difference formulas
records.description: Derive and apply sine, cosine, and tangent sum and difference formulas.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive and apply sine, cosine, and tangent sum and difference formulas.
Find cos 15 degrees exactly without a calculator. Angle addition supports exact values, rotations, signal combination, and derivation of double-angle formulas.

records.title: Double-angle formulas
records.description: Derive and use double-angle identities, including three equivalent cosine forms.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive and use double-angle identities, including three equivalent cosine forms.
Given sin theta=3/5 in quadrant II, find sin 2theta and cos 2theta exactly. Double angles appear in geometry, signal harmonics, power reduction, and equation solving.

records.title: Half-angle and power-reduction formulas
records.description: Derive half-angle and power-reduction identities and select signs using quadrant information.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive half-angle and power-reduction identities and select signs using quadrant information.
Given cos theta=-5/13 and theta in quadrant III, find sin(theta/2) and cos(theta/2). Half-angle identities support exact values, equations, and repeated angle subdivision.

records.title: Product-to-sum and sum-to-product formulas
records.description: Convert products and sums of trig functions to alternate forms and interpret signal combinations.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Convert products and sums of trig functions to alternate forms and interpret signal combinations.
Rewrite cos 7x+cos 3x as a product and identify the fast and slow factors. The formulas explain beats, interference, Fourier-style signal structure, and certain equation transformations.

records.title: Equations using fundamental identities
records.description: Solve trig equations by converting functions, factoring, and applying fundamental identities.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve trig equations by converting functions, factoring, and applying fundamental identities.
Solve sec x=2cos x on [0,2pi). Identity equations arise in waves, geometry, and transformed periodic models.

records.title: Quadratic-form trigonometric equations
records.description: Use substitution and algebraic solving for equations quadratic in a trig function.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use substitution and algebraic solving for equations quadratic in a trig function.
Solve 2sin^2 x-3sin x+1=0 on [0,2pi). Quadratic forms appear naturally after identities, harmonic combinations, and substitutions.

records.title: Multiple-angle equations
records.description: Solve equations involving sin(nx), cos(nx), or tan(nx) and translate solution families back to x.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve equations involving sin(nx), cos(nx), or tan(nx) and translate solution families back to x.
Solve sin(3x)=sqrt(3)/2 on [0,2pi). Multiple-angle equations model higher harmonics, repeated rotations, and oscillations with increased frequency.

records.title: General solutions and interval restrictions
records.description: Write complete periodic solution families and extract all solutions from specified intervals.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Write complete periodic solution families and extract all solutions from specified intervals.
Write all real solutions to cos x=-1/2, then list those in [-2pi,3pi]. General solutions are essential for periodic models and later differential equations.

records.title: Exact and numerical trigonometric equation solving
records.description: Use graphing, bracketing, and numerical methods for trig equations without convenient exact solutions.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Exact and numerical trigonometric equation solving
Use graphing, bracketing, and numerical methods for trig equations without convenient exact solutions.
Solve sin x=0.3x on [0,6] to three decimals. Numerical trig equations appear in engineering, signal timing, navigation, and nonlinear models.

records.title: Right triangles and trigonometric ratios
records.description: Connect unit-circle trig definitions with ratios in similar right triangles.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Connect unit-circle trig definitions with ratios in similar right triangles.
A ramp rises 0.84 meter over a horizontal run of 7.2 meters. Find its angle of inclination and length. Right-triangle ratios support slopes, heights, components, surveying, and geometric proofs.

records.title: Right-triangle applications
records.description: Model heights, distances, slopes, and angles of elevation or depression.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Model heights, distances, slopes, and angles of elevation or depression.

From a point 80 meters from a building, the angle of elevation to the roof is 37 degrees. The instrument is 1.6 meters high. Find building height. Applications include surveying, ramps, astronomy, construction, and navigation.

records.title: The Law of Sines
records.description: Derive and apply the Law of Sines to ASA, AAS, and suitable SSA triangles.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive and apply the Law of Sines to ASA, AAS, and suitable SSA triangles.
A triangle has A=42 degrees, B=71 degrees, and side a=18. Find sides b and c. The Law of Sines supports triangulation, navigation, astronomy, and surveying.

records.title: The ambiguous SSA case
records.description: Determine whether SSA data produce zero, one, or two triangles.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Determine whether SSA data produce zero, one, or two triangles.
Given A=35 degrees, a=8, and b=12, determine all possible triangles. The ambiguity matters in surveying and navigation when measurements do not uniquely locate a point.

records.title: The Law of Cosines
records.description: Use the Law of Cosines for SAS and SSS data and connect it to the Pythagorean theorem.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use the Law of Cosines for SAS and SSS data and connect it to the Pythagorean theorem.
Two sides of a triangle are 11 and 16 with included angle 124 degrees. Find the third side. The law supports distance, structural geometry, navigation, and vector magnitude calculations.

records.title: Triangle area formulas
records.description: Use K=(1/2)ab sin C and compare with base-height and Heron forms.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use K=(1/2)ab sin C and compare with base-height and Heron forms.
Find the area of a triangle with sides 9 and 14 enclosing 52 degrees. Triangle area supports surveying, design, force geometry, and coordinate calculations.

records.title: Bearings and navigation
records.description: Translate among standard angles, quadrant bearings, headings, and triangle or component models.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Translate among standard angles, quadrant bearings, headings, and triangle or component models.
A boat travels 18 km on bearing N35E, then 25 km on bearing S70E. Find its displacement magnitude and bearing. Bearings support aviation, maritime navigation, surveying, and search planning.

records.title: Vectors geometrically and in components
records.description: Represent vectors by magnitude and direction, add them geometrically, and convert to components.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Represent vectors by magnitude and direction, add them geometrically, and convert to components.
A force of 80 N acts at 135 degrees. Write its component vector. Vectors model displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, and data transformations.

records.title: Vector operations, magnitude, direction, and unit vectors
records.description: Use scalar multiplication, normalization, and component resolution.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Vector operations, magnitude, direction, and unit vectors
Use scalar multiplication, normalization, and component resolution.
A cable pulls with force <120,160> N. Find force magnitude and the unit vector in its direction. Unit vectors support navigation, force decomposition, coordinate bases, and matrix transformations.

records.title: Dot product, angles, and projection
records.description: Use the dot product to find angles, test orthogonality, and calculate projections.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use the dot product to find angles, test orthogonality, and calculate projections.
Find the angle between u=<2,5> and v=<4,-1>. Dot products model work, lighting, similarity, orthogonality, and directional influence.

records.title: Conics as loci and the circle foundation
records.description: Define loci by distance conditions and derive the standard circle equation.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Conics as loci and the circle foundation
Define loci by distance conditions and derive the standard circle equation.
Find the locus of points exactly 5 units from (-2,3) and determine its x- and y-intercepts. Circle loci support navigation, coverage, orbits, construction, and the geometric origin of trigonometry.

records.title: Parabolas from focus and directrix
records.description: Derive and analyze parabolas as points equidistant from a focus and directrix.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive and analyze parabolas as points equidistant from a focus and directrix.
Find the equation of points equidistant from focus (0,3) and directrix y=-3. Parabolic reflection explains satellite dishes, headlights, microphones, and projectile approximations.

records.title: Ellipses
records.description: Analyze ellipses from constant-sum distance and standard equations.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze ellipses from constant-sum distance and standard equations.
An ellipse has foci (-4,0),(4,0) and constant distance sum 10. Find its standard equation. Ellipses model orbits, acoustics, architecture, and constant-total-distance constraints.

records.title: Hyperbolas
records.description: Analyze hyperbolas from constant-difference distance and standard equations.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze hyperbolas from constant-difference distance and standard equations.

A hyperbola has center (0,0), vertices (±3,0), and foci (±5,0). Find its equation and asymptotes. Hyperbolas appear in navigation differences, cooling-tower sections, optics, and inverse-product graphs after transformation.

records.title: Completing squares in two variables
records.description: Convert general quadratic relations to standard conic form by completing squares.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Convert general quadratic relations to standard conic form by completing squares.
Classify and graph x^2+6x+4y^2-8y=11. The technique connects general quadratic equations to geometric conic parameters.

records.title: Translated conics and general equations
records.description: Classify translated conics and recover all geometric features from standard form.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Classify translated conics and recover all geometric features from standard form.
Classify 9x^2+4y^2-54x+16y+61=0 and find center, axes, and vertices. General equations arise from algebraic models, intersections, and coordinate changes.

records.title: Degenerate conics and classification
records.description: Identify point, line, pair-of-lines, empty-set, and other degenerate quadratic relations.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Identify point, line, pair-of-lines, empty-set, and other degenerate quadratic relations.
Describe the graph of x^2+y^2+4x-6y+13=0. Degenerate cases matter in parameter families, optimization boundaries, and algebraic classification.

records.title: Eccentricity and unified conic structure
records.description: Use eccentricity to compare circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use eccentricity to compare circles, ellipses, parabolas, and hyperbolas.
A conic has focus at (4,0), directrix x=9, and eccentricity 1/2. Determine its type and derive an equation. Eccentricity describes orbital shape, optical design, and a unified family of conics.

records.title: Nonlinear systems involving conics
records.description: Solve and interpret intersections of lines, circles, parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Solve and interpret intersections of lines, circles, parabolas, ellipses, and hyperbolas.
Find intersections of x^2+y^2=25 and y=x+1. Conic systems solve geometric design, collision, coverage, and path-intersection questions.

records.title: Conic models and applications
records.description: Construct and critique conic models in reflection, orbit, architecture, and navigation settings.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Construct and critique conic models in reflection, orbit, architecture, and navigation settings.
A satellite dish is 3.6 meters wide and 0.45 meter deep. Find focal distance. Conic modeling connects equations with physical design and scientific interpretation.

records.title: Parametric equations and orientation
records.description: Interpret x=f(t), y=g(t) as a directed path with a parameter interval.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Interpret x=f(t), y=g(t) as a directed path with a parameter interval.

For x=2t-1 and y=t^2, -2≤t≤3, find endpoints, direction, and the Cartesian curve. Parametric equations model motion, closed curves, projectiles, mechanical linkages, and paths that fail the vertical-line test.

records.title: Eliminating a parameter
records.description: Eliminate parameters while preserving interval restrictions and lost orientation information.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Eliminate parameters while preserving interval restrictions and lost orientation information.
Eliminate t from x=t+1, y=t^2-4 for -2≤t≤3. Elimination helps compare parametric and implicit representations and solve intersections.

records.title: Parametric motion and vector-valued position
records.description: Use r(t)=<x(t),y(t)> to describe position, displacement, and average velocity.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use r(t)=<x(t),y(t)> to describe position, displacement, and average velocity.
A particle has r(t)=<t^2-1,3t>. Find displacement and average velocity from t=1 to t=4. Vector-valued motion supports navigation, robotics, projectiles, and the later calculus of parametric curves.

records.title: Intersections, repeated points, and multiple parameter values
records.description: Distinguish curve intersections from self-intersections and repeated positions.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Intersections, repeated points, and multiple parameter values
Distinguish curve intersections from self-intersections and repeated positions.
For x=t^2-1,y=t^3-t, find all parameter values that produce (0,0). Repeated points matter in motion planning, curve design, and polar tracing.

records.title: Polar coordinates and nonuniqueness
records.description: Represent points as (r,theta), use negative radius, and generate equivalent polar coordinates.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Represent points as (r,theta), use negative radius, and generate equivalent polar coordinates.
Plot (-4,5pi/6) and give two equivalent representations with positive radius. Polar coordinates naturally describe rotation, radial symmetry, spirals, roses, and conics with a focus at the pole.

records.title: Cartesian and polar conversion
records.description: Convert points and equations using x=r cos theta, y=r sin theta, and r^2=x^2+y^2.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Convert points and equations using x=r cos theta, y=r sin theta, and r^2=x^2+y^2.
Convert the line x=4 to a polar equation and state where the formula is undefined. Conversion lets us choose whichever coordinate system exposes the structure most clearly.

records.title: Graphing polar equations
records.description: Trace r=f(theta) using tables, signed radius, and interval selection.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Trace r=f(theta) using tables, signed radius, and interval selection.
Trace r=2+2cos theta over 0≤theta≤2pi and identify intercepts and maximum radius. Polar tracing represents antennas, orbital shapes, petals, spirals, and directional measurements.

records.title: Polar symmetry and repeated tracing
records.description: Test symmetry and choose intervals that trace a polar curve exactly once.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Test symmetry and choose intervals that trace a polar curve exactly once.
Determine all standard polar symmetries of r=2cos(3theta) and an interval that traces it once. Symmetry reduces graphing work and reveals parameter structure.

records.title: Common polar families and polar conics
records.description: Analyze parameter effects in circles, cardioids, limacons, roses, lemniscates, spirals, and conics.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Common polar families and polar conics
Analyze parameter effects in circles, cardioids, limacons, roses, lemniscates, spirals, and conics.
Predict how the graph of r=1+2cos theta differs from r=2+cos theta. Polar families appear in optics, antenna patterns, planetary models, and decorative geometry.

records.title: Complex numbers in polar form
records.description: Represent complex numbers by modulus and argument and convert between rectangular and polar forms.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Represent complex numbers by modulus and argument and convert between rectangular and polar forms.
Write z=-3+3sqrt(3)i in polar form using a principal argument. Polar complex form connects algebra with rotations and scaling.

records.title: Complex multiplication, division, and powers
records.description: Multiply moduli, add arguments, divide moduli, subtract arguments, and apply De Moivre's theorem.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Multiply moduli, add arguments, divide moduli, subtract arguments, and apply De Moivre's theorem.
Compute [2cis(30 degrees)][3cis(80 degrees)] and interpret geometrically. Complex multiplication models rotations, oscillations, roots of polynomials, and electrical phasors.

records.title: Roots of complex numbers
records.description: Find all nth roots of a complex number and interpret their equal angular spacing.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Find all nth roots of a complex number and interpret their equal angular spacing.
Find all cube roots of 8i. Complex roots complete polynomial solution sets and create regular polygons in the complex plane.

records.title: Sequences as discrete functions
records.description: Interpret a sequence as a function on an integer index set.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Interpret a sequence as a function on an integer index set.
The first five terms are 4,7,12,19,28. Plot them as a discrete function and propose a formula. Sequences model samples, payments, populations, algorithms, and repeated experiments.

records.title: Explicit and recursive descriptions
records.description: Move among term lists, explicit formulas, recursive rules, tables, and plots.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Move among term lists, explicit formulas, recursive rules, tables, and plots.
A sequence begins 3,8,18,38,78. Write a recurrence and an explicit formula. Explicit-recursive translation supports algorithms, finance, population models, and discrete dynamics.

records.title: Arithmetic sequences
records.description: Derive and use a_n=a_1+(n-1)d and connect arithmetic sequences to sampled linear functions.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive and use a_n=a_1+(n-1)d and connect arithmetic sequences to sampled linear functions.

An auditorium has 18 seats in row 1 and 4 more seats in each later row. How many seats are in row 35? Arithmetic sequences model seating rows, straight-line depreciation, regular deposits, and evenly spaced measurements.

records.title: Geometric sequences
records.description: Derive and use a_n=a_1r^{n-1} and connect geometric sequences to sampled exponential functions.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Derive and use a_n=a_1r^{n-1} and connect geometric sequences to sampled exponential functions.

A bacteria count is 600 at hour 1 and triples every 2 hours. Write a sequence for counts at odd-numbered hours. Geometric sequences model compound growth, decay, rebounds, dilution, and repeated scaling.

records.title: Recurrence, iteration, and discrete dynamical models
records.description: Analyze repeated function application, fixed points, cycles, and qualitative long-run behavior.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Recurrence, iteration, and discrete dynamical models
Analyze repeated function application, fixed points, cycles, and qualitative long-run behavior.
A population follows P_{n+1}=0.6P_n+80 with P_0=50. Compute six terms and predict the limiting value. Discrete dynamics model populations, loans, feedback, algorithms, and control systems.

records.title: Sigma notation and finite sums
records.description: Interpret summation notation, index bounds, summands, and term counts.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Interpret summation notation, index bounds, summands, and term counts.
Expand and evaluate sum from k=2 to 6 of (3k-1). Sigma notation supports series formulas, probability, polynomial expansions, and numerical accumulation.

records.title: Arithmetic series
records.description: Derive and use S_n=n(a_1+a_n)/2.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Find the total number of seats in 35 auditorium rows when the first has 18 and each adds 4. Arithmetic sums model total seating, regular payments, stacked objects, and cumulative linear change.

records.title: Finite geometric series
records.description: Derive and use S_n=a_1(1-r^n)/(1-r).
records.label: Lesson
keywords: A ball rebounds to 70% of its previous height. Starting from 10 meters, find the total upward distance over the first 8 rebounds. Finite geometric sums model total rebounds, payments, repeated discounts, and digital scaling.

records.title: Infinite geometric series and convergence
records.description: Determine convergence and evaluate infinite geometric sums when |r|<1.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Determine convergence and evaluate infinite geometric sums when |r|<1.

A ball is dropped from 12 meters and rebounds to 3/4 of each previous height. Find its total vertical travel. Infinite geometric series model recurring decimals, rebounds, annuities, and self-similar constructions.

records.title: Mathematical induction
records.description: Prove statements for all integers in a domain using base case and inductive step.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Prove statements for all integers in a domain using base case and inductive step.
Prove 1+3+5+...+(2n-1)=n^2. Induction proves sum formulas, divisibility, inequalities, and recursive identities.

records.title: Pascal's triangle and binomial coefficients
records.description: Connect combinations, recursive construction, symmetry, and polynomial coefficients.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Connect combinations, recursive construction, symmetry, and polynomial coefficients.
Find the coefficient of x^4 in (2+x)^7 without expanding the whole polynomial. Binomial coefficients connect algebra, probability, combinatorics, and discrete models.

records.title: The binomial theorem and discrete-model synthesis
records.description: Expand binomial powers and compare arithmetic, geometric, recursive, and accumulated models.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: The binomial theorem and discrete-model synthesis
Expand binomial powers and compare arithmetic, geometric, recursive, and accumulated models.
Find the first four nonzero terms of (1-2x)^8. The binomial theorem supports probability, approximation, combinatorial identities, and polynomial structure.

records.title: Function-family classification
records.description: Classify unfamiliar formulas, graphs, tables, and contexts using structural evidence.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Classify unfamiliar formulas, graphs, tables, and contexts using structural evidence.

A graph is positive, decreasing, concave upward, has domain all reals, and approaches y=2 as x grows. Name plausible families and identify one additional feature needed. Family recognition is the organizing skill behind all of Precalculus and the first step in many Calculus problems.

records.title: Model selection and comparison
records.description: Select and compare function models using patterns, residuals, domains, and parameter meanings.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Select and compare function models using patterns, residuals, domains, and parameter meanings.

Three models fit the same ten data points: linear, exponential, and logistic. What evidence should decide among them? Model comparison supports scientific reasoning, economics, engineering, and data analysis.

records.title: Average rate of change revisited
records.description: Compare average rates across function families and interpret units and interval dependence.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Compare average rates across function families and interpret units and interval dependence.
Compare average rate of change of x^2, 2^x, and sin x from x=0 to x=1. Average rates bridge Precalculus models with derivative concepts.

records.title: Difference quotients
records.description: Construct and simplify [f(x+h)-f(x)]/h and interpret its components.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Construct and simplify [f(x+h)-f(x)]/h and interpret its components.
Simplify the difference quotient for f(x)=x^2-3x. Difference quotients are the algebraic raw material of derivatives.

records.title: Secant lines and tangent intuition
records.description: Interpret tangent slope as a limiting value of secant slopes.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Interpret tangent slope as a limiting value of secant slopes.
For f(x)=x^2 at x=2, calculate secant slopes using h=1,0.5,0.1,0.01 and predict the tangent slope. Secant-to-tangent reasoning motivates derivatives, velocity, and local approximation.

records.title: Local linearity and magnification
records.description: Recognize when a smooth graph appears linear under magnification and identify failures of local linearity.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Recognize when a smooth graph appears linear under magnification and identify failures of local linearity.

Zoom around x=1 on y=x^2 and build the tangent-line approximation from the predicted slope 2. Local linearity supports estimation, measurement error analysis, and the conceptual meaning of derivatives.

records.title: Intuitive limits
records.description: Estimate limits from tables, graphs, and algebra while distinguishing approached value from function value.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Estimate limits from tables, graphs, and algebra while distinguishing approached value from function value.
Evaluate the limiting value of (x^2-1)/(x-1) as x approaches 1, and compare with the function value at 1. Limits organize continuity, derivatives, asymptotes, and infinite processes.

records.title: Continuity and discontinuity
records.description: Classify removable, jump, infinite, and endpoint discontinuities using function values and limiting behavior.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Classify removable, jump, infinite, and endpoint discontinuities using function values and limiting behavior.
Choose k so that f(x)=(x^2-4)/(x-2) for x≠2 and f(2)=k is continuous. Continuity supports existence arguments, model reliability, and later theorems of Calculus.

records.title: Infinite behavior and asymptotes
records.description: Synthesize finite and infinite input behavior across polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric families.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Synthesize finite and infinite input behavior across polynomial, rational, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric families.
Compare x^3, 2^x, ln x, and sin x as x approaches infinity. Infinite behavior prepares students for limits, improper processes, and asymptotic model comparison.

records.title: Numerical approximation and sensitivity
records.description: Use bracketing, iteration, finite differences, and residuals while evaluating sensitivity to rounding and parameter error.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Use bracketing, iteration, finite differences, and residuals while evaluating sensitivity to rounding and parameter error.

A model predicts y=1000e^{0.08t}. Compare the time to reach 2000 when the rate is 0.08 versus 0.081. Numerical reasoning supports roots, regression, inverse models, engineering tolerances, and computational Calculus.

records.title: Accumulation, finite sums, and area preview
records.description: Connect rates, rectangles, finite sums, net change, and area under a rate graph.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Accumulation, finite sums, and area preview
Connect rates, rectangles, finite sums, net change, and area under a rate graph.

A pump's rate is 4,6,9,7 liters per minute over four one-minute intervals. Estimate total volume added using left-endpoint rectangles. Accumulation connects velocity to displacement, flow to volume, density to mass, and rates to totals.

records.title: Precalculus synthesis capstone
records.description: Analyze an unfamiliar multirepresentation problem by selecting and combining methods from the entire course.
records.label: Lesson
keywords: Analyze an unfamiliar multirepresentation problem by selecting and combining methods from the entire course.

A rotating sensor has position r(t)=<5cos t,5sin t>, signal strength S(t)=12e^{-0.1t}[1+0.2cos(3t)], and readings sampled every pi/6 time units. Determine domains, periods, decay behavior, selected positions, average signal change, and one appropriate limit question. The capstone demonstrates readiness to enter Calculus as a connected study of change and accumulation rather than a collection of new formulas.
